import "fmt"

	big := make([]int, 1000)
	small := big[10:12]
	fmt.Println(len(small))
	fmt.Println(cap(small))
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	rows := make([][]int, 2)
	base := []int{1}
	rows[0] = base
	rows[1] = base
	rows[0][0] = 9
	fmt.Println(rows[0][0])
	fmt.Println(rows[1][0])
}

package main

import "fmt"

func main() {
	dst := make([]int, 3)
	n := copy(dst, []int{3, 4})
	fmt.Println(n)
	fmt.Println(dst[0])
	fmt.Println(dst[2])
}
Why can a small subslice of a large array keep all that memory alive?
options: The header points at the same array; GC keeps the whole array object
The small slice’s len equals the large one’s
The subslice copies the whole array into the header

questions.text: Do string([]byte) and []byte(string) copy the bytes?
options: Yes. A string is immutable, so the bytes live in a separate array

How does slices.Delete differ from append(s[:i], s[j:]...) in the array tail?
options: The append trick zeros the tail; Delete does not
Both always allocate a new array
Delete zeros evicted elements; the append trick leaves old values past the new len

questions.text: What does json.Unmarshal("null", &s) do to slice s?
options: It leaves s as it was
It makes s empty but non-nil

questions.text: Why does writing v.Field in for _, v := range []*T change the elements?
options: v is a copy of the pointer, but it still points at the same struct
range always writes through to the original slice
It works only for nil pointers

questions.text: How do you drop a large array while keeping a few elements?
options: Copy the needed elements into a new slice (Clone/copy), or clip cap to len and stop holding the old header

questions.text: What does slices.Compare return when a is lexicographically less than b?
What does slices.Compact do?
options: It collapses consecutive equal elements to one, like unique on runs
It removes all duplicates in any order

questions.text: Where does slices.Reverse change elements?
options: In a new array; the original is untouched
In place, in the same array
Only in a copy of the header

questions.text: What does slices.BinarySearch do when the value is missing?
options: The index where it would be inserted, and found=false

questions.text: Why may two [][]int entries stop sharing an array after append on one of them?
options: append changes only the outer slice
If the inner slice’s cap is exhausted, append yields a new array; the other header still points at the old one

questions.text: What does append(dst, str...) do for []byte and string?
options: It appends the string’s bytes onto the byte slice
It replaces dst with the string

questions.text: Why call slices.Grow before a series of appends?
options: To grow cap ahead of time so each append does not reallocate

questions.text: What happens to an array if you take a[i:j] without a third index and then append?
options: append is forbidden on a slice from an array
If spare cap remains, the tail of the array is overwritten

questions.text: What does json.Unmarshal("[1,2]", &s) do to var s []int?
options: It is an error because s is nil
It writes only into cap and does not change len
It allocates a slice and fills in the elements

questions.text: What does slices.Index return when the element is missing?
Does slices.Sort mutate the original slice?
options: No, it returns a sorted copy

questions.text: Why does s[0:0:0]; append(..., x) not write s[0] of the original?
options: cap is clipped to 0, so append takes a new array

questions.text: What does slices.Replace(s, i, j, vs...) do when vs is longer than j-i?
options: It replaces using only the first j-i of vs
It inserts all vs values; the slice length grows

questions.text: A subslice big[i:j] can keep the whole big array alive.
string([]byte) shares the buffer with the original []byte, so a byte write changes the string.
json.Marshal yields null for a nil slice and [] for []T{}.
slices.Delete leaves old values in the tail past the new len, like the append trick.
json.Unmarshal("null", &s) sets the slice to nil.
In a range over []*T, writing v.Field changes the struct on the heap.
s = s[i:j] always lets GC drop the tail of a large array.
slices.Compare returns -1 when the first slice is less.
slices.Compact removes non-unique elements anywhere, not only consecutive ones.
slices.Reverse rearranges elements in place.
BinarySearch returns -1 when the element is missing.
append on one [][]int row can detach it from another row if cap is exhausted.
append([]byte, string...) is allowed and appends bytes.
slices.Grow immediately increases len by n.
append on a[i:j] without a third index can overwrite a’s tail if cap remains.
slices.Index returns -1 when the element is missing.
slices.Sort does not mutate the original slice.
s[0:0:0] then append writes the original s[0].
slices.Replace can grow length if more elements are put in than were cut.
[]byte(string) copies bytes; writing the slice does not change the string.
Why can small := big[i:j] keep all of big alive?
questions.answer: The header pointer refers to the same array; GC does not trim the array to the small slice’s cap.

questions.text: Does []byte(string) copy the data?
questions.answer: Yes. A string is immutable; the slice gets its own array.

questions.text: What does json.Marshal write for a nil slice and for []T{}?
Does slices.Delete zero the tail past the new len?
questions.answer: Yes, so references are not kept. The plain append trick does not.

questions.text: What does unmarshaling JSON null into *[]T do?
Why does ranging over pointers mutate the structs?
questions.answer: The pointer is copied; the object behind it is the same.

questions.text: How do you avoid keeping a large array alive with a small slice?
questions.answer: Copy the elements into a new slice, or clip cap (Clip / full slice) and drop the old header.

questions.text: What does slices.Compare return when a < b?
What does slices.Compact collapse?
Is slices.Reverse in-place?
questions.answer: Yes, it rearranges elements of the same array.

questions.text: What does BinarySearch return when the element is missing?
When do two [][]int rows stop sharing an inner array?
questions.answer: When append on one row exceeds its cap and allocates a new array.

questions.text: What does append(b, s...) do for []byte b and string s?
questions.answer: It appends the string’s bytes onto b.

questions.text: Does slices.Grow change len?
questions.answer: No, it prepares cap for later appends.

questions.text: What happens to array a after append on a[i:j] with no third index, if cap allows?
questions.answer: The array tail is overwritten by the new element.

questions.text: What does slices.Index return when the element is missing?
Does slices.Sort sort in place?
Why does append after s[:0:0] not write the old array?
questions.answer: Capacity is 0, so a new array is required.

questions.text: Can slices.Replace increase len?
questions.answer: Yes, if more elements are inserted than were cut.
